source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-18: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 18 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated test window, supported GPU/NIC hardware, and no production traffic. Treat GPUDirect RDMA as a hypothesis to verify, not a label inferred from throughput. Record GPU/NIC PCIe topology, NUMA and process affinity, peer-access capability, driver/firmware/runtime versions, link state, IOMMU and container permissions, buffer registration/pinning results, queue/completion errors, and an instrumented indication of whether transfers are direct or host-staged.

Hypothesis: with message size, placement, concurrency, duration, and software versions held fixed, an explicitly confirmed direct GPU-to-NIC path will improve effective bandwidth (GB/s) and/or reduce host CPU utilization versus an otherwise matched host-staged control, without increasing latency tails, errors, or data-integrity failures. Disconfirming evidence includes registration failure, unsupported topology, permission errors, a fallback/staging path, or no improvement beyond measurement uncertainty. Run interleaved randomized direct/control trials, warm up separately, synchronize transfer and completion timestamps, and verify payload checksums. Report message size (bytes), concurrency, duration (s), bandwidth (GB/s), latency (ms), host CPU (%), GPU utilization, PCIe/NIC counters, error counts, and p50/p95/p99 with sample counts and variability; compare confidence intervals or bootstrap intervals rather than a single best run.

Use a small authorized canary first and stop/rollback to the known-good staged path on data corruption, unbounded latency, link or completion errors, thermal/power instability, or agreed error/latency thresholds. Do not change IOMMU, firmware, routing, or container privileges during the measurement without recording it and obtaining authorization. A conclusion requires path-detection evidence, matched baseline results, correctness checks, and environment/version records; otherwise mark the result inconclusive and request the missing evidence.
risks: GPUDirect support and direct-path observability are platform- and software-dependent
host staging can be mistaken for direct transfer if path instrumentation is absent
benchmark results may be confounded by topology, NUMA placement, concurrency, or thermal state
evidence_required: interleaved matched baseline measurements with errors, correctness checks, and uncertainty
